Code claims verified literally: LearnModeTab.jsx:197-214 writes revvy_complete_*, revvy_review_schedule and strength (lib/strength.js is 100% localStorage) with no server counterpart; app/api/learn-mode/progress/route.js:37 and :57 upsert 'correct' / 'complete' / `post:${n}` into last_result, which scripts/create-practice-progress-table.sql:13 declares BOOLEAN (no later migration alters it); the route ignores the upsert result and returns {ok:true}; the client .catch(()=>{}) swallows; GET /api/learn-mode/progress has zero consumers (only reference in the codebase is LearnModeTab's POST). So the retention loop is device-bound and the one server write has never succeeded. Not refuted.

Why 'critical' is inflated under the first-3-sessions lens: (1) the loop only arms on completion, and live data shows completion is rare early (introductory-concepts: 15 completions vs 167 stuck at step 0), so for the majority the loop never exists to be lost; (2) a single-device student is entirely unaffected in sessions 1-3 — the schedule, strength bar, completion tick and review banner all work; (3) Safari's 7-day storage eviction only bites after a week away, i.e. beyond the 3-session window for an active user; (4) CompletionScreen.jsx (lines 95-140) never tells the student a 1/3/7/14-day review has been scheduled — the only review copy is 'Review flashcards' and 'Mixed review (N topics)' — so a device-switching student experiences a silent absence, not a visibly broken promise. The step itself IS server-persisted via /api/progress/content (StudyApp.jsx:423, :633-639), so on a second device a completed section shows 'You left off at step N of N' rather than being lost.

Real harm that survives: a logged-in student who completes a section on a school laptop and opens the phone next day gets no completion dot, no strength, no due-review banner, and a confusing 'resume at step N of N' banner for a section they finished; 'Mixed review' never unlocks because completedCount is read from the local schedule. International-school teens on laptop+phone are a plausible minority of completers, and completers are the users most likely to convert. Plus the endpoint is genuinely dead code that fails on every step navigation. Downgrade critical -> high.
